clue.text: Pronounce upon medical treatment

definitions.note: the definition is a verb meaning to speak out in an oratorical way

indicators.note: a treatment is a working-over, so the letters of medical are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor gives an opinion on what therapy a patient should receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon' is a link word; 'treatment' rearranges MEDICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to orate or speak out formally, much as one pronounces a judgement.

clue.text: Most inexpensive hat priced in error

indicators.note: something done in error is mistaken, so the letters of hat priced are muddled

explanation.surface: A hat on sale has been wrongly marked at a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges the nine letters of HAT PRICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirt-cheap costs almost nothing, so it is about as cheap as goods get.

clue.text: It may be seen smoking after hostilities

definitions.text: It may be seen smoking after hostilities

parts.words: It may be seen smoking after hostilities
parts.note: a Native American peace pipe was smoked to seal the end of fighting

explanation.surface: Something smouldering after a battle, like ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests burning wreckage; in fact it is the ceremonial pipe smoked when peace was made.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is the ceremonial tobacco pipe of North American peoples, shared to mark a truce.

clue.text: Ordered a charge on port facility

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are put into a new arrangement, here those of a charge on

explanation.surface: Someone was told to levy a fee on goods at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges A CHARGE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a place where ships can lie at anchor, a harbour amenity.

clue.text: Master card is a club

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A top player's card turns out to be a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy spiked staff used as a weapon, a kind of cudgel.

clue.text: Go back and negotiate again

explanation.surface: Retreating and reopening talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as RE-TREAT, to treat (negotiate) once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw; read as re-treat it means to bargain a second time.

clue.text: Balances books without any profit

explanation.surface: An accountant's balances show the books made no profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remainders are unsold copies of books cleared off cheaply, with no profit to the publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Remainders are what is left over, as balances are, and also surplus stock sold off at a loss.

clue.text: Bill is part of a bird, that goes without saying

indicators.note: one piece being part of another means it sits within it, so the bill goes inside the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A bird's beak is so obvious nobody mentions it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not the beak but AC, an account; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being stated.

clue.text: English people in rented accommodation offering appropriate environment

indicators.note: the people are placed in the rented accommodation, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a let is a property rented out
men can stand for people in general

explanation.surface: Housing English tenants in a rented flat gives them a suitable setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offering' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in one's element is to be in the surroundings that suit one best.

clue.text: Patient finally objects to nurses

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Patient

parts.note: ends are aims or objects

explanation.surface: A patient at last complains about the nursing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' looks like a verb of protest but means aims; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to look after the sick, as a nurse does.

clue.text: Soldiers left in charge of object of veneration

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Troops have been left guarding a sacred object.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a saint's remains or belonging, revered by the faithful.

clue.text: Arrive with fresh request for admission

parts.note: to arrive is to come
fresh linen is clean

explanation.surface: Someone turns up spruced up and asks to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' is not entry but confession; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to come clean is urging them to confess, a demand for an owning-up.

clue.text: Army leader wearing decoration is quite usual

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
MM is the Military Medal
clothes one is wearing are on

explanation.surface: A commander sporting a medal is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Common means ordinary or frequently met with.

clue.text: Girl's hair causing trouble

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A young woman is upset about her hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is anguish or difficulty.

clue.text: Deceptive motorway bend ahead

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
an S-bend is an S-shaped curve
a runner who is ahead is leading

explanation.surface: A road sign warns of a bend coming up on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London-to-Leeds motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Misleading means giving a false impression.

clue.text: Irregular player adding to the score

explanation.surface: A part-time player contributes to the team's total.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra is a film or stage walk-on; in cricket extras are runs not scored off the bat but still added to the total.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk-on actor is no regular cast member, and cricket's byes and wides are additional runs.

clue.text: Drew attention to article pocketed by accused

indicators.note: pocketed by means held inside, so the article goes within the word for accused

parts.note: indicted means formally charged
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone pointed out that the defendant had pocketed an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like an object stolen, but it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or signal something.

clue.text: Arrest in case is not ordered

indicators.note: ordered means rearranged, so case is not is put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A police arrest made where the case was not properly organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' means a halt, not a detention; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrest of movement is a stopping, an end or halt.

clue.text: Take up exercises inside, clad in blue

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another, so the exercises go into the word for clad

parts.note: clad means dressed

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means reading the word upwards, so exercises runs backwards

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in blue is told to take up indoor exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take up' turns the exercises upwards, as a down clue reads; 'clad' looks like part of the blue surface but supplies the outer word; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is feeling low, gloomy in spirits.

clue.text: A driver going round in circles?

definitions.text: A driver going round in circles?

parts.words: A driver going round in circles?
parts.note: a motorist lost and circling is the surface; the real driver is a spinning blade pushing a ship or plane along

explanation.surface: A lost motorist circling the same roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is what drives a vessel forward by rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw on a boat or aircraft drives it forward by turning rapidly.

clue.text: Perhaps bowled over — certainly surpassed

parts.note: a batter bowled is out, and someone bowled over is knocked out
Done! is a way of saying certainly, agreed

explanation.surface: A batter bowled out was definitely beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket being bowled is one way a batter is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outdone is to be beaten or bettered by a rival.

clue.text: Group riding organisation

parts.note: a set is a group
a jockey who is riding is up

explanation.surface: A riding club's set of members.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is an arrangement or structure, how something is run.

clue.text: Current State support for Crown Unit

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the state comes after the crown and unit

parts.note: the crown of something is its top
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit
CAL is short for California

explanation.surface: Present-day state backing for a Crown department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a noun about flow, but means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means of present interest, about current affairs.

clue.text: Food for West Country man?

explanation.surface: A dish from a man of the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bath chap is cured pig's cheek; Bath is a city in the West Country of England, so a chap from there.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is smoked or salted pork cheek; a man from that Somerset city fits the second reading.

clue.text: One giving a ring to Eastern beauty

parts.note: a bell gives a ring

explanation.surface: A man gives an engagement ring to an Oriental beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is not jewellery but a peal.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman.

clue.text: Creature' seen in Channel Islands eating cereal

indicators.note: one piece eating another holds it inside, so the cereal is taken in

parts.note: oat is a cereal

explanation.surface: An animal is spotted on the Channel Islands eating grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted mammal of the raccoon family.

clue.text: Lots following second test

indicators.note: following means the word for lots comes after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: ample means plenty, lots

explanation.surface: Many people resit an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample is to try or taste a bit, to check it.

clue.text: One expecting to broadcast, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir expects to inherit an estate or title.

clue.text: Contemplate quick movement order

parts.note: to contemplate is to look at
quick in the old sense means living

explanation.surface: Thinking about a fast movement command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Look alive! is a command to get moving and hurry up.

clue.text: Old Americans domiciled in Spain — Castile perhaps

indicators.note: domiciled in means living within, so the word lives inside the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Ancient Americans settled in a Spanish region like Castile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were a pre-Columbian people of Peru.

clue.text: Making plane before nightfall

explanation.surface: Building an aircraft until dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is not an aircraft but flat, so making level.
explanation.definitionFit: Making level or flat is evening up; the close of day before full dark is the evening.

clue.text: Doctor called back about joint, irritation having persisted

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned doctor surrounds the joint
called back means the abbreviation for doctor is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the ankle is a joint

explanation.surface: A GP rang back about an ankle injury that kept irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called back' reverses DR to RD, which goes 'about' ANKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rankled when it continued to cause resentment.
